physicalNotes: Radius 2.821 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104887: radius 2.821 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 10.659 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.092) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,962,570 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 6214 +/- 286 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104887: effective temperature 6214 +/- 286 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.256) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.

sources.position: Gaia DR3 source 1964791583368233088 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, A&A 674, A1), ICRS at epoch J2016.0, from the archived row src/objects/enduri-senggu/source/photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv; cross-identification HD 202444, HR 8130, HIP 104887: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=Gaia+DR3+1964791583368233088
sources.distance: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 104887: distance 20.342 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.008), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 20.342 +/- 0.163 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
sources.properMotion: Gaia DR3 source 1964791583368233088 is a two-parameter solution with no proper motion; zero is assumed (at 20 pc, 1 mas/yr would be 0 km/s across the sky)
sources.radialVelocity: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1964791583368233088 (quality A), from 2007AN....328..889K; Gaia DR3 measures none (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007AN....328..889K/abstract)
